newsitem.title: PERU: Peru military head lauds Fujimori's cool in crisis.
newsitem.headline: Peru military head lauds Fujimori's cool in crisis.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori, closely linked to the military throughout his seven years in office, received full praise on Thursday from Peru's armed forces' chief for his cool handling of the hostage crisis.
"The president kept control of the situation. He fixed the goals and the armed forces adopted the necessary measures," Gen. Nicolas Hermoza said.

Fujimori exhausted all options for a bloodless end to the 126-day siege at the Japanese ambassador's home before ordering the rescue of the Tupac Amaru rebels' hostages, Hermoza told mourners during the burial of two commandos killed in the raid.
"The president's first priority was to search for a peaceful solution without bowing down in any way that could have harmed the state's security," the general said.

Fujimori, in turn, lauded the work of the military and the intelligence service for freeing all but one of the 72 hostages held by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) in a meticulously planned and executed raid.

Hermoza, whose armed forces were caught off guard by the guerrillas when they stormed the Japanese ambassador's home on Dec. 17, avoided gloating over a raid that he said incurred a "minimum loss of life."
"Today we can say, without being too triumphal, that the mission achieved its aim," he said.
Security forces killed all 14 of the hostage-takers despite attempts by some rebels to give themselves up, according to an MRTA member who heard the raid on a short-wave radio channel.
